name: Belgium

observations.reasoning: Sourced on 2026-07-27, transversal pass over the population indicator. Population on 1 January 2025: 11883495 inhabitants, recorded as 11.883 million. Eurostat dataset demo_pjan, Population on 1 January by age and sex, read through the dissemination API on 2026-07-27, dataset last updated 2026-07-09. Total population, both sexes, all ages, which is exactly what this indicator's denominator asks for. Read as one table covering every country in the record, so no value here is derived from a neighbour: each is that country's own row. The previous value was an opening estimate produced with no source and no research.

Collected on 2026-07-28, in Dutch and French, in the transversal venues pass, and corrected the same day. Five units, four houses and one stage, against an opening estimate of 3.5 produced with no research. The first count was 7 and three of those seven were museums; the ruling that a museum programming shows is not a venue of diffusion and creation removed two of them and kept the third. Flanders gives two houses. FroeFroe plays at Namenstraat 7 in Antwerp, having taken its own artistic course inside the Koninklijk Jeugdtheater complex from the 1997-98 season and gained a multi-year structural subsidy under the arts decree. Beeldsmederij De Maan holds its own theatre at Minderbroedersgang 3 in Mechelen — a hall of 175 seats, a second of 124 and a café, in the restored Holy Spirit chapel and house — and is a vzw supported by the Flemish government, the city of Mechelen and the province of Antwerp. Two of the four structurally funded Flemish figure-theatre organisations are not counted, for the rule that counts these: Theater De Spiegel and Ultima Thule are companies, and Ultima Thule works in residence in other people's halls, De Spil's Komedie among them. Brussels gives two houses. The Théâtre Royal de Toone plays in the impasse Schuddeveld off the rue du Marché-aux-Herbes, is the only traditional Brussels puppet theatre still working, is inscribed on the Brussels inventory of intangible cultural heritage, and shows the Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles, the Région de Bruxelles-Capitale and the Ville de Bruxelles. The Théâtre Royal du Peruchet has played since 1929 and for more than fifty years in Ixelles, in an eighteenth-century farmhouse holding its theatre and a free puppet museum, with the support of the Communauté française stated on its own pages beside COCOF and the Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles. Peruchet keeps a museum and is not one: it is a theatre that has played for a century and shows its collection to its own audience. Liège gives the stage, and it is the discovery of the pass. The Théâtre Royal Ancien Impérial at the Musée Tchantchès, rue Surlet 56, is the oldest puppet theatre in the city. It is run by the asbl République Libre d'Outre-Meuse, whose vocation is the folklore of the quarter rather than puppetry alone, so it is a stage inside a larger organisation rather than a house. It holds two master puppeteers and a team of five manipulators and plays from October to the end of April, Sundays at 10h30 and Wednesdays at 14h30. That fixed weekly rhythm and that permanent troupe are why it survived the museum ruling while the other two did not: the museum is beside the theatre here, not the thing doing the programming. Two are removed and the removal is the point. The Théâtre de marionnettes du Musée de la Vie wallonne has carried the Liège tradition in the same room since 1931 and has its own programming from September to April, but it is a room in an ethnographic museum run by the Province de Liège, and a museum that programmes shows is not a venue of diffusion and creation. The Centre de la Marionnette de la Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles at rue Saint-Martin 47 in Tournai fails twice over: it is the French Community's designated puppetry centre and its Musée des Arts de la Marionnette, and its programming happens in the Créa-Théâtre rather than in a hall of its own. It is the most institutionally recognised puppetry body in French-speaking Belgium and it is not a venue. Five is a floor. Le Théâtre à Denis, given as a puppet museum and theatre in Liège, was not read and would have to pass the same test. The record is disputed on that and on Tchantchès, which is the one entry where the museum ruling had to be applied by judgement rather than by reading.

observations.reasoning: Web check of 2026-07-27, searched in the country's own language. One establishment retained, the value moving from 0.5 to 1: ARTS2 Mons, a higher arts school of the Wallonia-Brussels Federation. Criterion read at source: a master's in puppetry arts, a standalone 60-credit master's opened in September 2020, run jointly with the Academy of Fine Arts and the Puppet House in Tournai, with a teaching team of fifteen. Puppetry is the object of the award itself and the school reports to the higher education ministry of the French Community. Counted at the establishment carrying the award: the Tournai partnership does not make three schools. The previous 0.5 was the midpoint of an estimated range. Upper bound at 2: the check covered the Wallonia-Brussels Federation and did not cover Flemish arts higher education, where a course could exist under another name.

establishments.name: ARTS² — École supérieure des Arts de la Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles
establishments.description: The higher arts school of the French Community of Belgium. Its puppetry master's, opened in September 2020, is run jointly with the Academy of Fine Arts and the Puppet House in Tournai, and is the only state-backed puppetry qualification in Belgium's French-speaking system.
